question: Which of the following leaders was declared the Emperor of India by the sepoys during the Revolt of 1857?
solution:
**The correct answer is: b) Bahadur Shah Zafar.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bahadur Shah Zafar**

 
 
• This statement is **correct**. During the Revolt of 1857, Bahadur Shah Zafar, the last Mughal emperor, was declared the Emperor of India by the rebelling sepoys.
 
• The sepoys rallied under Bahadur Shah Zafar’s leadership as a symbolic figurehead to unify various factions against British rule.
 
• Based in Delhi, Bahadur Shah Zafar was an important unifying figure, even though he had limited practical power.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Other Options__**

__
 
• **Nana Saheb**

 
 
• Nana Saheb was a prominent leader in the 1857 revolt and led the uprising in Kanpur, but he was not declared the Emperor of India by the sepoys.
 
 
 
• **Rani Lakshmibai**
 
 
• Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi was a key leader in the revolt, known for her bravery, but she was not declared the Emperor of India. Her role was central in the resistance at Jhansi.
 
 
 
• **Tantia Tope**
 
 
• Tantia Tope was a close ally of Nana Saheb and a significant leader in the 1857 rebellion, particularly known for his tactical guerrilla warfare. However, he was not declared Emperor by the sepoys.
 
 

**Therefore, the correct answer is Option b) Bahadur Shah Zafar.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Role of Bahadur Shah Zafar in the Revolt of 1857:**__

 
 
• **Symbol of Unity:** Though he held limited actual power, Bahadur Shah Zafar’s position as the last Mughal emperor made him a powerful symbol for uniting various groups in India against British rule.
 
• **End of the Mughal Dynasty:** Following the suppression of the revolt, the British captured Bahadur Shah Zafar, exiled him to Rangoon, and formally ended the Mughal dynasty in India.
